_comment: VideoScribe settings. Edit this file to change the defaults for everyone
who uses this copy. To change something only on your own machine, copy
.env.example to .env and set it there instead -- .env always wins.
Any setting can also be overridden on the command line, which wins over both.
Language of the menus and messages: en or es.
Leave empty to follow the operating system, falling back to English.
The menu can change this for you and remembers the choice in .env

audio._comment: How the sound track is extracted.

_comment: model: tiny, base, small, medium, large-v3. Bigger is more accurate and
slower. Run 'python videoscribe.py models' to see timings for your computer.
language: two-letter code such as es or en, or auto to detect it.
cpu_threads: 0 means use every core, up to 16.
count: how many people speak. 0 asks the program to work it out, which is
unreliable in noisy recordings -- if the result looks wrong, set the real
number here and re-run with --resume, which takes seconds.
label: the word before the number, giving Person1, Person2, ...
Leave it empty to follow the interface language (Person / Persona).
The optional written account of what is visible on screen.
frame_interval_seconds: a frame every N seconds. Smaller catches more
detail and costs proportionally more.
window_seconds: how much video is described per request.
vision_model / synthesis_model: leave empty to use the sensible default
for whichever image model is configured.
output_language: the language the account is written in.
Folders, relative to this file unless you give a full path.
ffmpeg: leave empty to search automatically.
Temporary files are deleted after a successful run. Keep them if you plan
to re-run a step with --resume.
